purpose: log the three latent batching bugs found while building the T=16384 entry point, and the step-size measurement that explains why the batched run returned NaN

three_latent_bugs.bug: _a_vd is per-cosmology (n_cosmo entries) but was zipped against self.sample (T entries). zip() silently truncates, so _taurend_nu had n_cosmo entries and failed to broadcast for any T > n_cosmo.
three_latent_bugs.why_it_never_showed: bucket_by_k=True runs one k at a time with all cosmologies, so T == n_cosmo and the lengths happened to agree
three_latent_bugs.symptom_when_exposed: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (16384,1) (128,1) at _event_times

three_latent_bugs.bug: built one entry per row of _tau_grid, which is one row per cosmology, so length == n_cosmo rather than T
three_latent_bugs.fix: index by self.sample so it is per-trajectory

three_latent_bugs.bug: np.maximum(self._tau_end[:, None] - tau, 0.0). Once _tau_end became per-trajectory (T,) and tau is (T,), the [:, None] made it (T,1)-(T,) = (T,T).
three_latent_bugs.symptom_when_exposed: the coefficient dict reached 2051.5 MiB at T=16384, of which tau_rem alone was 2048 MiB, and the CUDA caching allocator aborted with NVML_SUCCESS == r INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED
three_latent_bugs.fix: removed the [:, None]; also deleted the dead ktau_rem line, which was never read after the switch moved onto the accumulated k*tau

verification_after_the_fixes.vram: allocated 3.8 MiB, reserved 26.0 MiB for T=16384

boundary_explosion.problem: evolve_torch takes the union of every trajectory's switch times. On one trajectory that is 6; on T=16384 the three families give 20897 (tc), 7158 (rsa_g) and 2890 (rsa_r) distinct values, so the union is 28366 boundaries and the run costs 32842 steps instead of 8060.
boundary_explosion.fix: merge boundaries closer than merge_tol in ln a
boundary_explosion.accuracy_cost_of_merging: on a single trajectory the merged run gives max rel diff 2.351e-3 against 2.328e-3 unmerged - negligible, because a single trajectory only has 6 switches and they do not merge

the_batched_run_returned_nan.run: T=16384 (128 k x 128 cosmologies), dlna=0.002, merge_tol=1e-2
the_batched_run_returned_nan.wall_time: 553.8 s, 8667 steps, 63.90 ms/step - matching the 8.8 min prediction
the_batched_run_returned_nan.consequence: the 14.2x device speedup computed from that run is VOID. No speedup is claimed for the batched path.

why_it_is_nan.isolation: T=128 at kmax=0.001 is fully finite (128/128); T=1024 at kmax=5 is 768/1024 finite; T=4096 at kmax=5 is 3371/4096 finite
why_it_is_nan.pattern: the failures cluster at k = 0.83..0.91 h/Mpc, so this is not a batching defect - it is the high-k trajectories diverging under a step that is far too coarse for them
why_it_is_nan.conclusion: the step needed spans a factor of 11 from k=0.05 to k=5. A batch must use ONE step, so it must use the smallest, and dlna=0.002 is twelve times too coarse for the k=5 end - which is exactly where the NaNs appear.

the_arithmetic_that_this_settles.cpu_path: bucket_by_k means every k gets its own adaptive step; across 128 k values the average is roughly 29000 steps, so 128 k x 128 cosmologies x 29000 steps at ~5.2 ms/step is ~2.5e6 s serial, or ~7.2 h on 96 cores
the_arithmetic_that_this_settles.gpu_path_with_one_uniform_step: the hardest k needs 97627 steps; at the measured 61.19 ms/step that is 5974 s, or 1.66 h
the_arithmetic_that_this_settles.ratio: about 4.3x in the GPU's favour - so the uniform-step batching strategy is not hopeless, it just costs a step twelve times smaller than the one used, which is why 553.8 s was a NaN and not a result
the_arithmetic_that_this_settles.the_catch: this is an estimate built from measured per-k step counts and a measured ms/step, not a completed run. The 97627-step batched run has not been executed, and at 1.66 h it is the next experiment, not a result.

what_may_be_claimed_now: rhs_torch is bit-identical to numpy: 0 of 229 state rows disagree
the segmented device integrator reaches 0.111% at dlna=0.002 on one trajectory (k=0.05, three state variables, z=0)
the GPU rhs is 3.76x faster than numpy at T=16384, and 10x slower at T=128
three latent batching bugs were found and fixed, taking the coefficient dict from 2051.5 MiB to 3.6 MiB
what_may_not_be_claimed: no GPU speedup for any end-to-end run: the only T=16384 run returned NaN
no batching entry point exists in power.py; bucket_by_k=True still runs T=1
the accuracy result is one k, one cosmology, three state variables - not P(k)
